newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were expected to open steady to 0.300 cent higher, livestock analysts said.
Evening up ahead of the monthly USDA cattle-on-feed report Friday afternoon is expected to dominate trade much of the day, analysts said.

Analysts also noted mixed opinions on cash cattle with some looking for a weak trend on expected larger fed supplies ahead while others noted anticipated strong demand for beef. Futures also remain discount to cash, they said.

Analyst estimates for May 1 on-feed numbers at the seven major feeding areas averaged 109.6 percent and ranged from 108 to 111 percent of last year. Placements averaged 113.9 percent and ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 while marketings averaged 101.0 and ranged from 98.6 to 104 percent.

May feeders were expected to continue its strong tone and should set a new high following another jump in the latest CME feeder cattle index. However, back months could again show price resistance, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $1.27 to $77.37 per cwt, highest level since August 23, 1994.
